target: area:langlands (part 3 of 3): CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility, EllipticCurveModularity, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions, PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp, SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation
summary: Four findings, all of missing mathematics, and one of them structural. The area's four construction roadmaps - R20, R29, R30, R31 - are in good order: their layers are source-bound, their boundaries are stated and, where two of them could overlap, they say which owns what. The weak point is ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions: all six of its stages are registries ('Execution state: specification'), yet 101 of the 143 missing items that accepted paper routes send into this area on source routes are addressed to them, from twenty extractions. The sharpest instance is Arthur's endoscopic classification for symplectic and orthogonal groups, with the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 and for SO(V): eight extractions route it here, no layer of the atlas constructs it, and the roadmap that owns endoscopic transfer says in its own summary that a classification of packets is not its endpoint. Two smaller gaps: the companion-forms theorem of Gross and Coleman-Voloch, which three extractions route to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3, and the completed cohomology of a definite quaternion algebra with its local-global compatibility, which Dospinescu-Le Bras routes into R31 with 26 items. Mechanical checks came back clean: every `requires` in the area resolves, and the boundaries between R30.6 and R31.4, between R20.2 and the Iwasawa 'Ribet's lemma' layers, and around Colmez's functor are each owned once. Disclosure: this session reviewed one of the thirty paper extractions routed into the area (PAPER-PILLONI-20, issue #1327). Finding 1 counts it among the eight extractions that route Arthur's classification here, but does not rest on it: the same items come from PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21, PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20, PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18, PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23, PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B, PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20, PAPER-ICHINO-PRASANNA-23 and PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20, none of which this session touched.
checked: All 30 stages of the five roadmaps with their full descriptions, requires and consumers, from research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/<id>.json, and the five roadmap summaries.
Every `requires` entry of every stage the area owns: all resolve to existing stages in data/atlas.json (0 unresolved).

The seven restructuring proposals that touch the area (RS-02, RS-06, RS-07, RS-08, RS-21, RS-26, RS-30), including their roadmaps, layers and owners lists; RS-21's owner assignment of general characteristic-zero local Langlands and inner-form comparison to EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6, and RS-26's boundary between PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp, PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology and PadicHodgeRegulators.
All 30 paper extractions routed into the area, their routes and route reasons, and every missing item they place on a source route into a layer of the area: 143 items in 14 route groups.

Catalogue-wide text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for: Arthur, Arthur's classification, multiplicity formula, Gan-Takeda, Adams-Johnson, endoscopy, local Langlands for classical groups, companion form, level lowering and Ribet, Colmez's functor, Serre modularity, local-global compatibility, definite quaternion, Bianchi, Ramanujan, imaginary quadratic modular forms.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison in full (its summary and the titles of its fifteen stages) and ET.6 in detail, to determine what the atlas does own of local Langlands for classical groups; AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6 (the invariant trace formula) and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2 (polarized systems on unitary groups) for the same reason.

Whether PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.6 and CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4 duplicate the local-global compatibility: they do not. R30.6 says 'All results here remain local; their occurrence inside global completed cohomology is the additional theorem of R31'. No finding.

Whether level lowering is planned twice: it is not. SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2 owns Mazur's principle and the Ribet/Diamond theorems; the other seventeen matches for 'Ribet' are the Iwasawa-theoretic Ribet's lemma (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.6 and its consumers), a different statement. No finding.
Whether Colmez's functor is planned twice: it occurs in exactly one stage, PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3. No finding.

findings.where: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 (and the atlas as a whole)
findings.claim: Arthur's endoscopic classification for symplectic and orthogonal groups - the packets and the multiplicity formula - together with the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan-Takeda) and for SO(V) (Vogan packets, Gan-Ichino), is constructed by no layer of the atlas, although eight accepted extractions route it to ML.4 and the atlas's GSp_4 modularity work depends on it.
findings.evidence: Eight extractions route these statements to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 on source routes: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI ('The local Langlands correspondence rec_GT for GSp_4 (Gan-Takeda)', 'Theorem 2.9.3: descent from GL_4 of symplectic type to GSp_4 by Arthur's multiplicity formula', 'The conditional status of Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4', 'Definition 2.3.1: the L-packet L(rho) of a GSp_4-valued Galois representation'), PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 ('Arthur's classification of the discrete spectrum of GSp4 (as used)', 'The archimedean Arthur packet of a general-type parameter'), PAPER-PILLONI-20 (the same two), PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 ('The local Langlands correspondence for SO(V) over all V (Vogan packets)', 'Arthur's multiplicity formula for non-split SO(V), generic parameters'), PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 ('The local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 (Gan-Takeda)'), PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B (six items on Xu's packets for PGSp_6), PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 ('Adams-Johnson packets are Arthur packets'), PAPER-ICHINO-PRASANNA-23 (the same for U(p,q)) and PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20. ML.4's description is a registry, not a construction: 'Give Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners: stabilization, transfer, fundamental lemma, packets, multiplicities and local-global compatibilities', with 'Execution state: specification; source-to-Lean decomposition and theorem-level dependency verification required', and its own acceptance criterion is that 'The symplectic torsion branch has a named source-verification/construction task'. No such task exists: a text search over all 1968 stage descriptions finds eleven stages mentioning Arthur, and none of them constructs the classification - AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.3/AS.6 build the invariant trace formula, EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4/ET.7 the stable and twisted unitary comparison, ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES7 and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5 the function-field parametrisation, TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.3 boundary induction. The endoscopy roadmap disclaims the scope explicitly in its summary: 'The global endpoint is the specified simple stable/twisted unitary comparison, not a claim of general Langlands functoriality or a classification of every packet.' Its local layer ET.6 is 'Classical local GL_m and inner-form comparison', and RS-21 assigns it exactly 'General characteristic-zero local Langlands and inner-form Jacquet-Langlands', not the classical-group correspondence. A search for 'Gan-Takeda' and for 'Adams-Johnson' returns no stage at all.
findings.fix: Give the endoscopic classification for classical groups a constructive owner and say what is assumed. Two ways are consistent with the atlas's practice. (a) Add a Part II of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison that owns the symplectic/orthogonal branch - the local Langlands correspondence for GSp_4 and SO(V), the packets and the multiplicity formula, with Arthur's and Xu's hypotheses retained - and have ML.4 register its statements rather than own them. (b) If the programme intends to treat Arthur's classification as an external, conditional input, say so in ML.4 in the form the extractions already use ('Arthur dependency registry', 'The conditional status of Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4'), and record it as an explicitly conditional prerequisite of every GSp_4 endpoint, so that no blueprint job downstream can mistake it for something the atlas will prove. What is not tenable is the present state: eight accepted routes address a construction task to a layer whose own text says it is a registry and whose acceptance criterion asks for a construction task that does not exist.

findings.claim: All six stages of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions are registry specifications, but 101 of the 143 missing items that accepted source routes send into this area are addressed to them; the routes ask a registry to own mathematics that no construction layer plans.
findings.evidence: Every ML stage ends 'Execution state: specification; source-to-Lean decomposition and theorem-level dependency verification required', and their construction lines are registrations: ML.0 'Define a common register of automorphic/Galois objects, coefficient fields, infinity types, local parameters, conductors and normalization conversions'; ML.1 'Organize Deligne-Serre Artin representations, weight-one modularity in proved cases'; ML.2 'Apply PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure with full regularity, polarization, residual-image, local and field-extension hypotheses'; ML.3 'Integrate Newton-Thorne source-scoped symmetric-power automorphy'; ML.4 'Give Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners'; ML.5 'Register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers'. Counting the missing items that accepted source routes place on ML stages: 101, from twenty extractions (ALLEN-ETAL-23, BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-25, BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25, BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25, BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 and -25, CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 and -20, CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20, CLOZEL-THORNE-17, FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22, FRESAN-SABBAH-YU-22, GAN-ICHINO-18, GAN-SAVIN-23 and -23-B, ICHINO-PRASANNA-23, JIANG-ZHANG-20, NEWTON-THORNE-26, PILLONI-20, QIAN-23). The largest clusters are Arthur and classical-group classification (finding 1, 37 items across ML.0/ML.4/ML.5), potential automorphy and symmetric powers (PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23, PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17, PAPER-QIAN-23, PAPER-FRESAN-SABBAH-YU-22, PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS, PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26, PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18: 59 items), and the Bianchi cluster of PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25 ('Bianchi modular forms, their Fourier coefficients and parabolic cohomology with Hecke action', 'Theorem E: the Ramanujan bound for Fourier coefficients of Bianchi eigenforms', 'Theorem G: mass equidistribution for level-one Bianchi eigenforms', 'The Jacquet-Shalika bound'), for which a text search over all stage descriptions finds Bianchi forms only in AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L2/L5, which are about p-adic L-functions, and no stage at all for the Ramanujan or Jacquet-Shalika bounds in this sense.
findings.fix: Decide, for each ML stage, whether it is a registry or a construction layer, and route accordingly. Concretely: keep ML.0 and ML.4 as registries and move the mathematics they are being asked for to construction owners - finding 1 for the classical-group classification; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.* for the potential-automorphy items ML.2 collects, which is where the routes' own reasons say the machinery lives; and a named owner for the Bianchi package (Fourier coefficients and parabolic cohomology of Bianchi eigenforms, the Jacquet-Shalika bound and the Ramanujan bound that follows from potential automorphy), for which ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces or a Part II of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions are the candidates. Then re-run the affected routes so that each item names the layer that will build it, rather than the register that lists it.

findings.claim: The companion-forms theorem of Gross and Coleman-Voloch - that a mod p modular representation unramified at p with T_p acting by the trace has a companion form of the complementary weight, equivalently the weight-one characterisation - is planned by no layer, although three accepted extractions route it to R20.3.
findings.evidence: Three extractions route companion-form items to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 on source routes: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 ('Companion forms force a split local representation'), PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 ('Weight-one mod p eigenforms: rho-bar unramified at p with T_p = trace (Gross; Coleman-Voloch)') and PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 ('Companion forms and weight lowering for mod l modular forms unramified at l (Gross; Coleman-Voloch)'). R20.3's description plans a different theorem: 'Prove the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem with its characteristic-p operations, local finite-flat/extension calculations and geometric interpretation. Include the reducible and irreducible local cases and all low-characteristic corrections that belong to the chosen theorem. State the exact conclusion at weight p+1 and the effect of twisting.' A text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for 'companion form' returns nothing.
findings.fix: Name the companion-forms theorem in R20.3 alongside the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem, with its sources (Gross's 1990 theorem and the Coleman-Voloch treatment of p = 2,3) and the hypotheses the three papers use - ordinariness at p, the unramified case and the split/non-split consequence for the local representation at p. It is the natural companion of what R20.3 already plans and its consumers are inside this area (weight-one forms in ML.1 and the modularity-lifting inputs of R32).

findings.claim: The completed cohomology of a definite quaternion algebra and Emerton's local-global compatibility for it are planned by no layer, although PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 routes 26 missing items about exactly those objects into R31.1/R31.2/R31.4.
findings.evidence: PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 (Dospinescu-Le Bras, Revetements du demi-plan de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands p-adique, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 321-411) routes 26 missing items to CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.1/R31.2/R31.4, among them 'Definition 4.3 (p-adic automorphic forms on the definite quaternion algebra B-bar)', 'Lemma 4.5 (Hom_{K_p}(W^*, C^0(X)) = A_{K_p}(W))', 'The Hecke algebras T_Sigma, T-tilde_Sigma(K_p) and T-tilde_Sigma', 'Definition 5.3 (the localized Hecke algebra A)', 'The Galois representation r^m over A and the Banach representations Pi(p)', 'Theorem 5.4 (Emerton's local-global compatibility for B-bar)' and 'Proposition 13.5 (the weak local-global statement)'. The three layers plan the GL_2/Q case: R31.1 'Specialize CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.0-CC.8 to modular/Shimura curves', R31.2 the classical specialisations and locally algebraic vectors, and R31.4 'the source theorem identifying the local p-adic representation attached to the Galois representation inside completed cohomology', whose 'concrete initial branch is Emerton's unpublished 2011 manuscript, Theorem 1.2.1' for a two-dimensional promodular representation of G_Q. The word 'quaternion' does not occur in R31.4, and the roadmap summary is explicit about the boundary: 'Keep the construction compatible with future completed cohomology over other number fields, but do not assert their local-global compatibility by analogy.' Elsewhere the atlas has the finite-level quaternionic theory - HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.4 includes 'the relationship between definite and indefinite quaternionic realisations supplied by Jacquet-Langlands' - but no layer builds the completed cohomology of a definite quaternion algebra or its local-global compatibility.
findings.fix: Add a layer to CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility for the definite quaternionic tower: the space of p-adic automorphic forms on B-bar as continuous functions on the finite adelic quotient, its Hecke algebras and localisations, the attached Galois representation and Banach representations, and Emerton's local-global compatibility in that setting, importing the finite-level Jacquet-Langlands comparison from R18.4. The alternative, a Part II of the roadmap, is heavier than the material warrants, since R31.1 already imports the quaternionic finite-level input. Whichever is chosen, the roadmap's own instruction not to assert local-global compatibility by analogy means the quaternionic statement must be proved, not inherited from the GL_2/Q branch.
